column1: # Brazilian Portuguese (pt-br) catalog. Columns, separated by a TAB:  context <TAB> source <TAB> translation
#   context  empty                a plain UI string; `source` is the English text in the code
#            @id                  a command id (e.g. file.saveAs): wins over the English text for
#                                 that menu item, so one id can read differently from its twin
#                                 the same two forms, so the translation is "one|other" too (see
#            anything else        a disambiguating context passed to `tr_ctx`
#   escapes  \n  \t  \\  inside a column. `{name}` placeholders must appear in both columns.
#   lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
# Clean-room: every entry was written from the plain meaning of the English label using ordinary
# Brazilian Portuguese computing vocabulary (arquivo, camada, caminho, preenchimento, traçado,
# pincel, amostra, prancheta ...), following common desktop-software conventions (commands
# in the infinitive, menus as nouns); no proprietary localisation resource, string table or product
# UI was consulted or copied; add entries the same way. Product and technology names (VectorCraft,
# ArtCraft, SVG, OpenType, CMYK, Lab ...) stay in Latin letters; the trailing "…" of dialog
# Coverage: the whole interface (every menu string and every `tl!` literal, `complete_menus`,
# `untranslated_report` lists gaps) and the status and error messages (`@msg` rows, `COMPLETE_MESSAGES`, `untranslated_report` lists gaps). Left in
# English on purpose (`MENU_KEEP_AS_IS` in the tests): the product name, language names, OpenType,
# the built-in workspace names and the bracketed perspective grid preset names.
